paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. God cares about how His people live, down to what's on the table and what they touch. He sorted the animals into clean and unclean, and He said the reason right there in the text: "For I am the LORD your God; consecrate yourselves, therefore, and be holy, because I am holy." (Leviticus 11:44) The whole list points back to Who is giving it.

God also says, "For I am the LORD, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt so that I would be your God; therefore be holy, because I am holy." (Leviticus 11:45) That's not a stranger barking orders at a crowd. That's the God who already rescued them, and He's asking the people He saved to live like they belong to Him. I think that's a good word for any baker today: the rescue comes first, and the holy living follows.

And the law ends with a job: "You must distinguish between the unclean and the clean…" (Leviticus 11:47) Even the small, daily things, like what they ate and what they touched, were a way to remember they were set apart for God. So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery, friend: pay attention to the little choices of your day, because the God who is holy is the One who called you. The teaching on clean and unclean isn't over, so keep that apron on.
